answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with slashing for fraud: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital, not just free keypairs. Like nectar drawn from a single oasis, value flows only through staked accounts, and a prism of peer attestations refracts each newcomer's history: newcomers start with low trust limits until established agents vouch for them, so a sybil swarm cannot mint reputation out of thin air.
